c324.title: Supercontinent Nuna
c324.detail: An era when the continents gathered into one. A supercontinent long before Pangaea.
c324.label: About 1.8 billion years ago

c325.title: Origin of Mitochondria
c325.detail: The organelle that makes energy inside eukaryotic cells. Said to have originally been a separate bacterium.
c325.label: About 1.5 billion years ago

c326.title: Origin of Sexual Reproduction
c326.detail: A mechanism for mixing genes arose, and the pace of evolution is said to have quickened.
c326.label: About 1.2 billion years ago

c327.title: Ancestors of Sponges
c327.detail: The ancestors of animals are thought to have been sponge-like organisms with hardly any body tissue.
c327.label: About 800 million years ago

c328.title: Marinoan Glaciation
c328.detail: The second snowball-Earth event, following the Sturtian glaciation.
c328.label: About 640 million years ago

c329.title: Gaskiers Glaciation
c329.detail: After the ice age, life diversified greatly, and the Ediacaran biota appeared.
c329.label: About 580 million years ago

c330.title: Kimberella
c330.detail: An early animal that was bilaterally symmetrical, with a front and back.
c330.label: About 550 million years ago

c331.title: Rise of Trilobites
c331.detail: Arthropods with hard shells diversified in the Cambrian seas. They fossilize easily and serve as markers of age.
c331.label: About 530 million years ago

c332.title: Chengjiang Biota
c332.detail: A fossil group in Yunnan, China. Even soft-body structures are preserved, conveying the Cambrian explosion in detail.
c332.label: About 520 million years ago

c333.title: Great Ordovician Biodiversification
c333.detail: The variety of marine life increased greatly over tens of millions of years. Corals and cephalopods flourished.
c333.label: About 480 million years ago

c334.title: Growth of Coral Reefs
c334.detail: Corals built reefs under the sea, becoming homes for many organisms.
c334.label: About 450 million years ago

c335.title: Animals Come Ashore
c335.detail: Arthropods such as centipedes and spiders followed the plants that had gone ashore first.
c335.label: About 430 million years ago

c336.title: Cooksonia
c336.detail: One of the oldest vascular plants. A mechanism for carrying water through the body made larger land plants possible.
c336.label: About 420 million years ago

c337.title: Jawed Fishes
c337.detail: Fishes with jaws and teeth appeared, predators increased, and marine ecosystems grew complex.
c337.label: About 420 million years ago

c338.title: Late Devonian Extinction
c338.detail: Many marine organisms died out. Falling temperatures and decreasing oxygen are thought to be the causes.
c338.label: About 370 million years ago

c339.title: Diversification of Sharks
c339.detail: Cartilaginous fishes flourished, and the lineages leading to modern sharks and rays split.
c339.label: About 340 million years ago

c340.title: Giant Dragonfly Meganeura
c340.detail: An insect with a wingspan of about 70 cm. The high oxygen levels of the time are said to have supported its size.
c340.label: About 300 million years ago

c341.title: Dimetrodon
c341.detail: A synapsid characterized by a sail on its back. Not a dinosaur; closer to the distant ancestors of mammals.
c341.label: About 280 million years ago

c342.title: Mid-Permian Extinction
c342.detail: Cooling from volcanic activity and falling oxygen are said to have wiped out many organisms.
c342.label: About 260 million years ago

c343.title: Siberian Traps
c343.detail: Huge volcanic activity continued in what is now Siberia. Said to be one cause of a mass extinction.
c343.label: About 250 million years ago

c344.title: Triassic Recovery
c344.detail: After the great extinction, survivors diversified and new ecosystems were built.
c344.label: About 250 million years ago

c345.title: Eoraptor
c345.detail: One of the oldest dinosaurs. Fossils were found in Argentina. A small, bipedal carnivorous dinosaur.
c345.label: About 230 million years ago

c346.title: Ancestors of Turtles
c346.detail: Fossils of creatures with a shell in an intermediate stage of development have been found in China.
c346.label: About 220 million years ago

c347.title: Breakup of Pangaea
c347.detail: The supercontinent split apart and the Atlantic began to open, leading to today's arrangement of continents.
c347.label: About 200 million years ago

c349.title: Stegosaurus
c349.detail: A herbivorous dinosaur with plates on its back and spikes on its tail. Its brain was small.
c349.label: About 160 million years ago

c350.title: Start of the Cretaceous
c350.detail: A warm climate and high sea levels spread shallow seas into continental interiors.
c350.label: About 140 million years ago

c351.title: Marsupial–Placental Split
c351.detail: Among mammals, the lineage with a placenta branched off.
c351.label: About 120 million years ago

c352.title: Spinosaurus
c352.detail: A giant carnivorous dinosaur that caught fish at the water's edge.
c352.label: About 100 million years ago

c353.title: Spread of Flowering Plants
c353.detail: Flowering plants spread rapidly, and coevolution with insects advanced.
c353.label: About 100 million years ago

c354.title: Mosasaurs
c354.detail: Giant reptiles at the top of Cretaceous seas. Related to lizards.
c354.label: About 80 million years ago

c355.title: Triceratops
c355.detail: A herbivorous dinosaur with three horns. Lived in the same age as Tyrannosaurus.
c355.label: About 68 million years ago

c356.title: Deccan Traps Volcanism
c356.detail: Large-scale eruptions continued in India. Along with the asteroid impact, said to have contributed to the mass extinction.
c356.label: About 66.05 million years ago

c357.title: Mammals Expand
c357.detail: After the dinosaurs departed, mammals spread into the vacant environments.
c357.label: About 65 million years ago

c358.title: Oldest Bats
c358.detail: Mammals that fly on wings had appeared by this time.
c358.label: About 52 million years ago

c359.title: Darwinius
c359.detail: The primate fossil "Ida" found in Germany. Nearly the whole body is preserved.
c359.label: About 47 million years ago

c360.title: Isolation of Antarctica
c360.detail: Australia drifted away, ocean currents encircling Antarctica formed, and the ice sheet grew.
c360.label: About 35 million years ago

c361.title: Animals of the Grasslands
c361.detail: Grass-covered plains spread and horses and ruminants flourished.
c361.label: About 23 million years ago

c362.title: Miocene Warm Period
c362.detail: Temperatures temporarily rose and forests spread north.
c362.label: About 15 million years ago

c363.title: Diversification of the Apes
c363.detail: Various apes flourished in Europe, Asia and elsewhere.
c363.label: About 11 million years ago

c364.title: Split from the Gorilla Lineage
c364.detail: The lineage leading to humans is thought to have branched from a line close to gorillas.
c364.label: About 8 million years ago

c365.title: Ardipithecus kadabba
c365.detail: An early human fossil found in Ethiopia. May have walked on two legs.
c365.label: About 5.8 million years ago

c366.title: Zanclean Flood
c366.detail: The Mediterranean is said to have reconnected with the Atlantic, and seawater poured into the dried-up basin.
c366.label: About 5.3 million years ago

c367.title: Australopithecus anamensis
c367.detail: An early human that walked on two legs. Fossils were found in Kenya.
c367.label: About 4.2 million years ago

c368.title: Australopithecus afarensis
c368.detail: The species Lucy belongs to. Its brain was about chimpanzee size, but it walked upright.
c368.label: About 3.9 million years ago

c369.title: Quaternary Ice Age
c369.detail: An age of alternating glacial and interglacial periods began. Said to have spurred human evolution.
c369.label: About 2.6 million years ago

c370.title: Paranthropus
c370.detail: Humans with robust jaws and teeth. Thought to have eaten mainly hard plant foods.
c370.label: About 2.5 million years ago

c371.title: Homo ergaster
c371.detail: A human that walked and ran on long legs. Regarded as an early form of Homo erectus.
c371.label: About 1.8 million years ago

c372.title: Turkana Boy
c372.detail: A nearly complete skeletal fossil of a boy found in Kenya.
c372.label: About 1.6 million years ago

c373.title: Change in Ice Age Cycles
c373.detail: The cycle of ice ages shifted from about 40,000 years to 100,000 years.
c373.label: About 1 million years ago

c374.title: Homo heidelbergensis
c374.detail: A human regarded as close to the common ancestor of Neanderthals and Homo sapiens.
c374.label: About 600,000 years ago

c375.title: Sima de los Huesos
c375.detail: Bones of about 30 individuals, ancestors of the Neanderthals, were found in a cave in Spain.
c375.label: About 430,000 years ago

c376.title: Acheulean Culture Develops
c376.detail: Well-shaped hand axes were made in many places.
c376.label: About 350,000 years ago

c377.title: Jebel Irhoud
c377.detail: The oldest Homo sapiens fossils, found in Morocco.
c377.label: About 315,000 years ago

c378.title: Everyday Use of Fire
c378.detail: People cooked with fire, making meat and plants easier to eat with heat. Said to have supported brain development.
c378.label: About 250,000 years ago

c379.title: Omo Kibish
c379.detail: Homo sapiens fossils found in Ethiopia.
c379.label: About 195,000 years ago

c380.title: Eemian Interglacial
c380.detail: Warmer than today, with sea levels several meters higher.
c380.label: About 130,000 years ago

c381.title: Oldest Burials
c381.detail: Traces of burials with grave goods have been found at sites such as Qafzeh Cave in Israel.
c381.label: About 100,000 years ago

c382.title: Katanda Bone Tools
c382.detail: Bone tools thought to be harpoon points were found in the Congo.
c382.label: About 90,000 years ago

c383.title: To Southeast Asia
c383.detail: Homo sapiens spread along the coasts and reached Southeast Asia.
c383.label: About 60,000 years ago

c384.title: Interbreeding with Neanderthals
c384.detail: The genomes of modern Europeans and Asians contain genes from Neanderthals.
c384.label: About 50,000 years ago

c385.title: Into Europe
c385.detail: Homo sapiens, such as Cro-Magnons, spread into Europe.
c385.label: About 45,000 years ago

c386.title: Sulawesi Cave Painting
c386.detail: A painting of a pig found in Indonesia. Among the oldest figurative paintings.
c386.label: About 45,000 years ago

c387.title: Bone Flute
c387.detail: In a cave in Germany, a flute made from a vulture bone was found. Music has ancient roots.
c387.label: About 40,000 years ago

c388.title: Denisovans
c388.detail: A finger bone found in Siberia revealed the existence of a new human group.
c388.label: About 33,000 years ago

c389.title: Sewing Needle
c389.detail: Needles made of bone stitched fur clothing together. They helped people spread into cold lands.
c389.label: About 30,000 years ago

c390.title: Sungir Site
c390.detail: At a site in Russia, graves of people wearing bead-decorated clothing were found.
c390.label: About 28,000 years ago

c391.title: Mammoth-Bone Houses
c391.detail: On the cold steppe, people built dwellings from assembled mammoth bones.
c391.label: About 24,000 years ago

c392.title: Spread of the Bow and Arrow
c392.detail: Bows and arrows came into wide use, making hunting more efficient.
c392.label: About 20,000 years ago

c393.title: Jericho
c393.detail: The town of Jericho in Palestine had one of the oldest settlements with stone walls and a tower.

c394.title: Domestication of Sheep and Goats
c394.detail: Wild animals were tamed to obtain meat, milk and wool.

c395.title: Domestication of Cattle
c395.detail: Livestock usable for farming and milking. They supported human life and society.

c396.title: Irrigation Farming
c396.detail: Water drawn from rivers to fields made agriculture possible even in dry lands.

c397.title: Winemaking
c397.detail: Jars in which grapes were fermented have been found at a site in Georgia.

c398.title: Copper Mining
c398.detail: The work of digging and processing metal began to grow in scale.

c399.title: Horse Husbandry
c399.detail: At the Botai site in Kazakhstan, traces of keeping horses have been found.

c400.title: Sailing Ships
c400.detail: On the Nile, boats with sails that move by wind began to be used.

c401.title: Bronze
c401.detail: An alloy of copper and tin. Hard and excellent as a material for weapons and farm tools.

c402.title: Unification of Egypt
c402.detail: Narmer and others unified Upper and Lower Egypt, and the dynasties began.

c403.title: Egyptian Solar Calendar
c403.detail: Based on the rising of Sirius and the Nile flood, they made a calendar with a 365-day year.

c404.title: Pyramids and Astronomy
c404.detail: The faces of the Great Pyramid align almost exactly with the cardinal directions. Star observations are thought to have been used.

c405.title: Epic of Gilgamesh
c405.detail: The tale of a Mesopotamian king and his friend. One of the world's oldest works of literature.

c406.title: Eruption of Santorini
c406.detail: A volcano in the Aegean erupted hugely, dealing a blow to the Minoan civilization.

c407.title: Egyptian Sundial
c407.detail: Tools that tell the time by the length of shadows were used in Egypt.

c408.title: Water Clock
c408.detail: In Egypt, tools measuring time by the amount of water flowing out were used.

c409.title: Rise of the Alphabet
c409.detail: The Phoenicians made a 22-letter script representing sounds, later passed to Greece and Rome.

c410.title: Babylonian Astronomical Diaries
c410.detail: In Babylon, records of stars, planets and eclipses were kept every night, accumulating centuries of observations.

c411.title: The Pythagoreans
c411.detail: They thought the order of the world could be expressed by ratios of numbers and found harmony in musical scales and the heavens.

c412.title: Anaxagoras
c412.detail: He thought the Sun was a burning stone and the Moon reflected sunlight.

c413.title: Democritus's Atomism
c413.detail: He thought the world is made of indivisible particles, "atoms," and void.

c414.title: Euclid's Elements
c414.detail: A book organizing geometry as proofs from axioms. Read as a mathematics textbook for over 2,000 years.

c415.title: Archimedes
c415.detail: He discovered much in mathematics and physics, beginning with the principle of buoyancy.

c416.title: Hipparchus's Star Catalog
c416.detail: He recorded the positions and brightness of about 850 stars and expressed stellar brightness in magnitudes.

c417.title: Hypatia
c417.detail: A woman mathematician and astronomer of Alexandria.

c418.title: Brahmagupta and Zero
c418.detail: Indian mathematicians set out rules for treating zero as a number.

c419.title: Al-Biruni Measures the Earth
c419.detail: He devised a method of measuring Earth's radius from the height of a mountain and the angle of the horizon.

c420.title: Roger Bacon
c420.detail: He argued for a science that values observation and experiment.

c421.title: Cusanus's Infinite Universe
c421.detail: He stated that the universe has neither center nor edge. A thought predating Copernicus.

c422.title: Regiomontanus Observes a Comet
c422.detail: He attempted to measure a comet's path. It is later known as Halley's Comet.

c423.title: Copernicus's Commentariolus
c423.detail: In the Commentariolus, he first wrote out the Sun-centered theory briefly.

c424.title: Tycho Observes a Comet
c424.detail: He measured parallax and showed the comet lies beyond the Moon. The idea of solid celestial spheres began to waver.

c425.title: Galileo's Pendulum
c425.detail: Watching a lamp swing in a church, he is said to have noticed that a pendulum's period does not depend on the width of its swing.

c426.title: Bruno's Infinite Universe
c426.detail: He asserted that the universe extends infinitely and that the stars are suns like our own.

c427.title: Discovery of Variable Star Mira
c427.detail: It became known that a star's brightness changes, overturning the idea of unchanging heavens.

c428.title: Invention of the Telescope
c428.detail: The Dutch spectacle maker Lippershey applied for a patent.

c429.title: Kepler's Harmonic Law
c429.detail: He discovered that the square of a planet's orbital period is proportional to the cube of its orbit's size.

c430.title: Observing the Transit of Venus
c430.detail: Horrocks observed Venus crossing in front of the Sun.

c431.title: Hevelius's Map of the Moon
c431.detail: He drew the Moon's craters and mountain ranges precisely.

c432.title: Huygens and Saturn's Rings
c432.detail: He clarified that the shape around Saturn is a ring.

c433.title: Hooke's Micrographia
c433.detail: It depicted the world seen through a microscope. The source of the word "cell."

c434.title: Greenwich Observatory
c434.detail: Founded in England to measure longitude for navigation.

c435.title: Newton's Opticks
c435.detail: He showed, among other things, that light splits into colors through a prism.

c436.title: Discovery of Aberration
c436.detail: Bradley found the apparent shift in stars' positions due to Earth's orbital motion.

c437.title: Return of Halley's Comet
c437.detail: As Halley predicted, the comet returned. It demonstrated the predictive power of Newtonian mechanics.

c438.title: Messier Catalog
c438.detail: Messier listed nebulae and clusters that got in the way of comet hunting. Still used by amateur astronomers today.

c439.title: Herschel's Milky Way
c439.detail: By counting stars, he inferred that the Milky Way has a disk shape.

c440.title: Cavendish Experiment
c440.detail: Using lead spheres, he measured the gravitational constant and determined Earth's mass.

c441.title: Discovery of Infrared
c441.detail: Herschel split sunlight with a prism and found light beyond red that is felt as heat.

c442.title: Young's Interference Experiment
c442.detail: It showed that light has wave properties.

c443.title: Lord Rosse and Spiral Nebulae
c443.detail: With a large telescope he found that some nebulae have a spiral shape.

c444.title: Foucault's Pendulum
c444.detail: It proved Earth's rotation by the rotation of the pendulum's plane of swing.

c445.title: Discovery of Helium
c445.detail: In the spectrum of sunlight, lines of an element unknown on Earth were found.

c446.title: Martian "Canals"
c446.detail: Schiaparelli announced he had seen lines on Mars, which sparked the spread of the Martian theory.

c447.title: Harvard Classification of Stars
c447.detail: Women classified stellar spectra, building a foundation for astronomy.

c448.title: Tsiolkovsky's Rocket Equation
c448.detail: He derived a formula for the speed needed for a rocket to reach space from the amount of fuel.

c449.title: Tunguska Event
c449.detail: An object exploded in the sky over Siberia, flattening 2,000 square kilometers of forest.

c450.title: First Liquid-Fuel Rocket
c450.detail: Launched by Goddard in the United States.

c451.title: Fusion as the Stars' Energy Source
c451.detail: Bethe and others explained the reaction turning hydrogen into helium at stellar cores.

c452.title: Trinity Test
c452.detail: The first nuclear explosion test. Humanity obtained the energy of the stars.

c453.title: Radar to the Moon
c453.detail: Radar was bounced off the Moon and its echo received, starting the era of measuring distances to celestial bodies by radar.

c454.title: Oort Cloud
c454.detail: It was proposed that the outer edge of the solar system holds a cloud of countless icy bodies.

c455.title: Photographing the Far Side of the Moon
c455.detail: The Soviet Luna 3 took the first photographs of the Moon's far side seen by humans.

c456.title: Project Ozma
c456.detail: The first attempt to search for radio signals from extraterrestrials.

c457.title: Mariner 2
c457.detail: The first probe to approach and observe another planet (Venus).

c458.title: First Spacewalk
c458.detail: The Soviet Leonov went outside into space and floated for about 12 minutes.

c459.title: Luna 9 Lands on the Moon
c459.detail: The first probe to soft-land on the Moon. It confirmed that the lunar ground is firm.

c460.title: Mariner 9
c460.detail: The first probe to enter orbit around another planet (Mars).

c461.title: Viking 1 and 2
c461.detail: They landed on Mars and searched for traces of life.

c462.title: Voyager 1 at Jupiter
c462.detail: It discovered volcanic activity on Jupiter's moon Io.

c463.title: First Space Shuttle Flight
c463.detail: The first launch of a reusable spacecraft.

c464.title: IRAS Satellite
c464.detail: It observed the whole sky in infrared and found about 350,000 objects.

c465.title: Exploring Halley's Comet
c465.detail: Several probes, including Japan's Sakigake and Suisei, approached Halley's Comet.

c466.title: Magellan Probe
c466.detail: It mapped the surface of Venus in detail by radar.

c467.title: Martian Meteorite ALH84001
c467.detail: It was announced that structures possibly showing traces of life were found in a meteorite of Martian origin.

c468.title: Mars Pathfinder
c468.detail: It sent the small rover Sojourner to Mars.

c469.title: International Space Station
c469.detail: Nations began building it cooperatively. Humans have lived continuously in space ever since.

c470.title: Sloan Digital Sky Survey
c470.detail: A project to digitally measure a wide area of the night sky and make a three-dimensional map of galaxies.

c471.title: Spirit and Opportunity
c471.detail: They found evidence of liquid water once existing on Mars.

c472.title: Huygens Probe
c472.detail: It landed on Saturn's moon Titan.

c474.title: Kepler Space Telescope
c474.detail: It searched for planets crossing in front of stars and found thousands of exoplanets.

c475.title: Planck Satellite
c475.detail: It measured the cosmic background radiation precisely and derived the universe's age as about 13.8 billion years.

c476.title: Curiosity
c476.detail: It landed in Gale Crater on Mars and confirmed that an environment habitable by life once existed.

c477.title: Gaia Satellite
c477.detail: A satellite measuring the positions and motions of a billion stars. It is making a three-dimensional map of the Milky Way.

c478.title: Pluto Flyby
c478.detail: New Horizons made its closest approach to Pluto and photographed icy mountains and the "heart" terrain.

c479.title: Planet Nine Hypothesis
c479.detail: From biases in the orbits of outer solar system objects, it was suggested that there may be an undiscovered large planet.

c480.title: Gravitational Waves and Light Together
c480.detail: A neutron star merger was observed in both gravitational waves and electromagnetic waves. The origin of heavy elements such as gold was confirmed.

c481.title: ʻOumuamua
c481.detail: Confirmed as the first object to come from outside the solar system.

c482.title: Perseverance
c482.detail: It collects Martian rocks, taking the first step of a plan to bring them to Earth.

c483.title: Ingenuity
c483.detail: The first aircraft (helicopter) to fly on another planet.

c484.title: Artemis I
c484.detail: An uncrewed test flight around the Moon. The first step of the Artemis program of crewed lunar exploration.

c485.title: OSIRIS-REx Sample Return
c485.detail: Samples brought back from asteroid Bennu reached Earth.

c486.title: SLIM Lunar Landing
c486.detail: Japan landed on the Moon with pinpoint accuracy.

c487.title: ISS Planned Retirement
c487.detail: The International Space Station is planned to end its service around 2030.
c487.label: Approx. 2030

c488.title: Europa Clipper Arrival (planned)
c488.detail: A probe to explore the ocean beneath the ice of Jupiter's moon Europa.
c488.label: Approx. 2030

c489.title: Dragonfly Arrival (planned)
c489.detail: A probe that will fly and study Saturn's moon Titan.
c489.label: Approx. 2034

c490.title: Transit of Venus
c490.detail: Venus crossing in front of the Sun. The next ones are in 2117 and 2125.

c491.title: Comet Swift–Tuttle
c491.detail: A comet with an orbital period of 133 years. There is no worry of it hitting Earth.

c492.title: Approach of Bennu
c492.detail: Asteroid Bennu will come near Earth around 2182. The chance of impact is said to be about one in several thousand.

c493.title: Change of Pole Star
c493.detail: Because of precession, the pole star is replaced by Alderamin in Cepheus.

c494.title: One Cycle of Precession
c494.detail: Earth's rotation axis traces a circle over about 26,000 years. The way constellations look comes full circle.
c494.label: About 26,000 years from now

c495.title: Voyager's Journey
c495.detail: The Voyager probes keep drifting among the stars even after their power runs out.
c495.label: About 3.6 million years from now

c496.title: End of Total Solar Eclipses
c496.detail: The Moon recedes bit by bit and can no longer cover the Sun completely.
c496.label: About 600 million years from now

c497.title: Plants Struggle to Live
c497.detail: The Sun brightens and carbon dioxide decreases, so many plants are predicted to find it hard to live.
c497.label: About 800 million years from now

c498.title: Cooling of Earth's Interior
c498.detail: Earth's interior may cool and its magnetic field weaken.
c498.label: About 2 billion years from now

c499.title: The Sun Brightens Further
c499.detail: The Sun will be about 40% brighter than now, and Earth is predicted to approach an environment like Venus.
c499.label: About 3.5 billion years from now

c500.title: Fate of the Earth
c500.detail: Whether Earth will be swallowed as the Sun expands is still unclear.
c500.label: About 7.6 billion years from now

c501.title: Isolation of Galaxies
c501.detail: Light from distant galaxies will no longer arrive, and only the Milky Way and its surroundings will be the visible universe.
c501.label: About 20 billion years from now

c502.title: Age of Red Dwarfs
c502.detail: Small stars burn slowly, so they keep shining for trillions of years.
c502.label: About 10 trillion years from now

c503.title: The Stars' Last Glow
c503.detail: Even after star birth ends, red dwarfs and others glow like embers.
c503.label: About 50 trillion years from now

c504.title: Disappearance of the Mediterranean
c504.detail: The African continent approaches Europe, and the Mediterranean is predicted to close.
c504.label: About 50 million years from now

c505.title: Loss of Saturn's Rings
c505.detail: The ice making up the rings is predicted to fall into Saturn or scatter and vanish.
c505.label: About 100 million years from now

c506.title: Increase in the Sun's Brightness
c506.detail: The Sun's light is expected to strengthen by about 10%, and evaporation of Earth's oceans to advance.
c506.label: About 1.1 billion years from now

c507.title: Disruption of Mercury's Orbit
c507.detail: Over long timescales, Mercury's orbit may be disturbed, with a slight chance of planetary collision.
c507.label: About 4 billion years from now

c508.title: Fate of Cosmic Expansion
c508.detail: The nature of dark energy will determine the fate of the universe. Research continues.
c508.label: About 30 billion years from now

aristotle.name: Aristotle
aristotle.detail: Systematized a cosmos with the celestial bodies revolving around Earth, long the foundation of the Western view of the universe.
aristotle.lesson: He tried to explain the world through observation and logic.

aristarchus.name: Aristarchus
aristarchus.detail: Said to be the first to propose that Earth revolves around the Sun.
aristarchus.lesson: Even an idea ahead of its time survives if it is recorded.

eratosthenes.name: Eratosthenes
eratosthenes.detail: Calculated Earth's size from the difference in the Sun's angle at two places.
eratosthenes.lesson: Everyday measurements can tell us the size of the Earth.

ptolemy.name: Ptolemy
ptolemy.detail: Mathematically systematized the geocentric model in the Almagest, which was used for about 1,400 years.
ptolemy.lesson: Precise calculation can be useful even from a wrong premise.

copernicus.name: Copernicus
copernicus.detail: Systematically laid out the Sun-centered theory and changed the view of the universe.
copernicus.lesson: Our view of the world can be changed with courage.

tycho.name: Tycho Brahe
tycho.detail: Left the most accurate naked-eye observational data of his time.
tycho.lesson: Precise data prepares the next theory.

kepler.name: Kepler
kepler.detail: Discovered the three laws of planetary motion from Tycho's data.
kepler.lesson: He found laws within the data.

galileo.name: Galileo Galilei
galileo.detail: Observed lunar mountains, Jupiter's moons and the phases of Venus with a telescope, supporting heliocentrism.
galileo.lesson: Confirm it with your own eyes.

newton.name: Newton
newton.detail: Set out the law of universal gravitation and the laws of motion, explaining that celestial bodies and earthly objects obey the same laws.
newton.lesson: Great discoveries stand on the shoulders of predecessors.

laplace.name: Laplace
laplace.detail: Explained the origin of the solar system by the nebular hypothesis and brought celestial mechanics near completion.
laplace.lesson: The power of calculation reaches even the universe.

darwin.name: Darwin
darwin.detail: Proposed evolution by natural selection and created a framework to explain the history of life.
darwin.lesson: Life, too, has a long history.

maxwell.name: Maxwell
maxwell.detail: Wrote the equations unifying electricity, magnetism and light, and showed that light is an electromagnetic wave.
maxwell.lesson: Seemingly separate phenomena can be united as one.

planck.name: Planck
planck.detail: Introduced the idea that energy takes discrete values, opening the door to quantum theory.
planck.lesson: A small correction can become a great revolution.

einstein.name: Einstein
einstein.detail: Transformed the understanding of time, space and gravity with special and general relativity.
einstein.lesson: Imagination can matter more than knowledge.

bohr.name: Bohr
bohr.detail: Explained the structure of the atom with quantum theory and became a central figure in the interpretation of quantum mechanics.
bohr.lesson: Dialogue with opposing ideas sharpens a theory.

hubble.name: Hubble
hubble.detail: Showed that the Andromeda Nebula lies outside the Milky Way, and showed the expansion of the universe by observation.
hubble.lesson: Beyond the telescope lay the vastness of the universe.

lemaitre.name: Lemaître
lemaitre.detail: Derived cosmic expansion from general relativity and thought the universe began from a primordial state.
lemaitre.lesson: Theory can picture the universe before observation does.

gamow.name: Gamow
gamow.detail: Laid the foundations of Big Bang theory and predicted the origin of the elements and the cosmic background radiation.
gamow.lesson: Playful thinking can hit upon the truth.

hoyle.name: Hoyle
hoyle.detail: Proponent of the steady-state theory, also known as the one who coined the name "Big Bang."
hoyle.lesson: An opponent's words can end up sticking.

rubin.name: Vera Rubin
rubin.detail: Provided strong evidence for dark matter from observations of galaxy rotation speeds.
rubin.lesson: She did not overlook the oddity in the data.

penrose.name: Roger Penrose
penrose.detail: Showed mathematically that black holes inevitably form under general relativity, and won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics.
penrose.lesson: Mathematics can speak of the universe's necessity.

susskind.name: Susskind
susskind.detail: Contributed to the development of the holographic principle and string theory.

hawking.name: Hawking
hawking.detail: Showed that black holes emit radiation and advanced research on the beginning of the universe and quantum gravity.
hawking.lesson: Even with bodily limits, thought can reach the universe.

thooft.name: Gerard 't Hooft
thooft.detail: Proposed the holographic principle and contributed greatly to particle physics theory. Nobel Prize in Physics 1999.
thooft.lesson: The world's information may lie on its boundary.

bekenstein.name: Bekenstein
bekenstein.detail: Proposed that a black hole's entropy is proportional to its surface area, opening the way to the holographic principle.
bekenstein.lesson: A bold intuition opens new physics.

guth.name: Alan Guth
guth.detail: Proposed inflation theory and popularized the idea of rapid expansion in the early universe.
guth.lesson: An inspiration can begin on a single page of a notebook.

maldacena.name: Maldacena
maldacena.detail: Proposed the AdS/CFT correspondence, widely studied as a concrete realization of the holographic principle.
maldacena.lesson: Separate theories may be different views of the same world.

schrodinger.name: Schrödinger
schrodinger.detail: Gave the equation governing the wave function, and sharply raised the measurement problem with his "cat" thought experiment.
schrodinger.lesson: How a question is posed sharpens a theory.

heisenberg.name: Heisenberg
heisenberg.detail: Built quantum mechanics with matrix mechanics and the uncertainty principle.

everett.name: Everett
everett.detail: Proposed the many-worlds interpretation, in which the wave function does not collapse.
everett.lesson: A heretical idea can later become part of the mainstream.

bell.name: John Bell
bell.detail: With Bell's inequality, made the debate over the foundations of quantum mechanics testable by experiment.
bell.lesson: He turned philosophy into a question for experiment.

witten.name: Witten
witten.detail: Proposed M-theory and led the "second revolution" in superstring theory.
witten.lesson: Connecting what looked separate into one.

antiframe.name: Anti-Frame
antiframe.detail: An anonymous proponent wearing a hood and gas mask. Published the Anti-Frame Theory on January 9, 2026, adding the "overwhelming agency of the observer" to the measurement problem. Now based at not/on.
antiframe.lesson: The observer is at the center of the question.

thales.name: Thales
thales.detail: Held that water is the origin of all things, one of the first to try to explain the world by natural principles rather than myth.
thales.lesson: From myth to explanation of nature.

pythagoras_c.name: Pythagoras
pythagoras_c.detail: Tried to understand the universe through the harmony of numbers; also credited with the idea that Earth is a sphere.
pythagoras_c.lesson: He saw the universe's order in the world of numbers.

hipparchus.name: Hipparchus
hipparchus.detail: Made a star catalog, discovered precession and laid foundations of trigonometry. Called the "Father of Astronomy."
hipparchus.lesson: An accumulation of precise observations yields new discoveries.

zhangheng.name: Zhang Heng
zhangheng.detail: Said to have explained the motions of heavenly bodies with an armillary sphere and built a seismoscope to detect earthquake direction.
zhangheng.lesson: He sought to understand both the heavens and earthquakes through observation.

aryabhata.name: Aryabhata
aryabhata.detail: Discussed the idea that Earth rotates and found pi precisely.
aryabhata.lesson: Ancient Indian astronomy was at a high level.

alsufi.name: Al-Sufi
alsufi.detail: Wrote the Book of Fixed Stars and recorded the Andromeda Galaxy and the Large Magellanic Cloud.
alsufi.lesson: He wrote down galaxies visible to the naked eye at the earliest date.

alhaytham.name: Ibn al-Haytham
alhaytham.detail: Studied the nature of light and the mechanism of vision by experiment in the Book of Optics. Also called the "Father of Modern Optics."
alhaytham.lesson: He nurtured a scientific method of confirming by experiment.

shenkuo.name: Shen Kuo
shenkuo.detail: Recorded a wide range of things in Dream Pool Essays, including magnetic declination and observations of strata.
shenkuo.lesson: Breadth of curiosity gave rise to an encyclopedia.

khayyam.name: Omar Khayyam
khayyam.detail: Took part in calendar reform (the Jalali calendar) and also studied equations as a mathematician. Also known as the poet of the Rubaiyat.
khayyam.lesson: He was both a poet and a calculator of calendars.

guoshoujing.name: Guo Shoujing
guoshoujing.detail: Devised instruments such as the simplified armillary and made the Shoushi calendar.
guoshoujing.lesson: Improved instruments raised the calendar's accuracy.

ulughbeg.name: Ulugh Beg
ulughbeg.detail: Built an observatory in Samarkand and precisely measured the positions of about 1,000 stars.
ulughbeg.lesson: A ruler became a patron of learning.

bruno.name: Giordano Bruno
bruno.detail: Asserted that the universe is infinite and that stars are bodies like the Sun. Declared a heretic and burned at the stake.
bruno.lesson: Ideas that see too far ahead live next to danger.

huygens.name: Huygens
huygens.detail: Discovered Saturn's rings and Titan and made the pendulum clock practical. Also proposed the wave theory of light.
huygens.lesson: He achieved observation, theory and machinery all by himself.

romer.name: Rømer
romer.detail: Observed eclipses of Jupiter's moons and showed the speed of light is finite.
romer.lesson: He estimated the speed of light from celestial observation.

halley.name: Halley
halley.detail: Worked out a comet's period from past records and predicted its return. The comet bears his name.
halley.lesson: The power of comparing records predicted the future.

w_herschel.name: William Herschel
w_herschel.detail: Discovered Uranus and observed many nebulae and double stars. He was originally a musician.
w_herschel.lesson: A musician became an explorer of the sky.

c_herschel.name: Caroline Herschel
c_herschel.detail: Assisted her brother William and discovered eight comets. The first woman astronomer to receive payment from the Crown.
c_herschel.lesson: From assistant in observation to discoverer.

fraunhofer.name: Fraunhofer
fraunhofer.detail: Recorded the dark lines in sunlight (Fraunhofer lines) and made high-performance lenses and spectroscopes.
fraunhofer.lesson: Precision optics opened the door to reading the makeup of stars.

bessel.name: Bessel
bessel.detail: Measured the annual parallax of 61 Cygni, the first measured distance to a star.
bessel.lesson: The measuring of cosmic distances began here.

leverrier.name: Le Verrier
leverrier.detail: Calculated the position of an unknown planet from irregularities in Uranus's orbit, leading to the discovery of Neptune.
leverrier.lesson: A planet found at the tip of a pen.

leavitt.name: Henrietta Leavitt
leavitt.detail: Discovered the relation between the brightness and period of variable stars, opening the way to measuring distances to faraway galaxies. It underlies Hubble's discovery of the expanding universe.
leavitt.lesson: An observatory "computer" made the yardstick of the cosmos.

payne.name: Cecilia Payne
payne.detail: Showed that most of a star is made of hydrogen and helium. It was not accepted then but later confirmed.
payne.lesson: Trust results that defy convention if the data are right.

shapley.name: Shapley
shapley.detail: From the distribution of globular clusters, showed the Milky Way's size and that the Sun is not at its center.
shapley.lesson: The Sun was not the center of the galaxy.

friedmann.name: Friedmann
friedmann.detail: Derived expanding-universe solutions from Einstein's equations. Died at 37.
friedmann.lesson: He shook the static-universe common sense with equations.

chandrasekhar.name: Chandrasekhar
chandrasekhar.detail: Calculated the upper mass limit of white dwarfs and showed the fate of stars in theory. Won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1983.
chandrasekhar.lesson: A young man's calculation predicted the fate of stars.

zwicky.name: Zwicky
zwicky.detail: First pointed to dark matter from observations of galaxy clusters, and proposed theories of supernovae and neutron stars.
zwicky.lesson: A point made decades early was overlooked.

penzias.name: Penzias
penzias.detail: Discovered the cosmic background radiation while tracing noise in an antenna. Won the 1978 Nobel Prize in Physics with Wilson.
penzias.lesson: Chasing noise, he found the light of the universe's beginning.

sagan.name: Carl Sagan
sagan.detail: Conveyed the wonder of the universe to the public through Cosmos, and researched extraterrestrial life and planetary exploration. Known for the "Pale Blue Dot."

oort.name: Jan Oort
oort.detail: Showed the rotation of the Milky Way and proposed the "Oort cloud," the source of long-period comets.
oort.lesson: From galactic rotation to the edge of the solar system.

kimura.name: Hisashi Kimura
kimura.detail: Discovered the "Z term" showing wobble of Earth's axis in latitude observations, and was internationally recognized. First director of the Mizusawa Latitude Observatory.
kimura.lesson: A Japanese astronomer contributed to the world.

asada.name: Asada Goryu
asada.detail: Accurately predicted eclipses from observation, and his disciples later contributed to improving the shogunate's calendar.
asada.lesson: Accuracy of observation made prediction possible.

inoh.name: Ino Tadataka
inoh.detail: Began studying astronomy at age 50 and spent 17 years surveying all of Japan, making a precise map.
inoh.lesson: It is never too late to start learning.

koshiba.name: Masatoshi Koshiba
koshiba.detail: Observed neutrinos from Supernova 1987A with Kamiokande, a world first, and won the 2002 Nobel Prize in Physics.
koshiba.lesson: A giant water tank caught particles from space.

itokawa.name: Hideo Itokawa
itokawa.detail: Father of Japanese rocketry. Started with the "Pencil Rocket"; the asteroid Hayabusa later visited is named for him.
itokawa.lesson: Space development began with a small rocket.

faraday.name: Faraday
faraday.detail: Discovered electromagnetic induction and introduced the idea of electric and magnetic "fields." Born into a poor family, he rose from bookbinder's apprentice to scholar.
faraday.lesson: Self-taught, he created the view of the field.

kelvin.name: Lord Kelvin
kelvin.detail: Proposed absolute temperature and calculated Earth's age from its cooling, but because radioactivity was unknown, it came out far too short.
kelvin.lesson: A wrong calculation was a harbinger of new discovery.

boltzmann.name: Boltzmann
boltzmann.detail: Built statistical mechanics and explained entropy through probability. Laid the basis of the idea of the "arrow of time."
boltzmann.lesson: He explained the direction of time by probability.

hertz.name: Hertz
hertz.detail: Confirmed the existence of electromagnetic waves by experiment. The unit of frequency, the hertz, is named for him. Died at 36.
hertz.lesson: He demonstrated the predicted electromagnetic waves by experiment.

rontgen.name: Röntgen
rontgen.detail: Discovered X-rays and won the first Nobel Prize in Physics.
rontgen.lesson: An unseen light imaged the inside of the body.

rutherford.name: Rutherford
rutherford.detail: Discovered the atomic nucleus and built the theory of radioactive decay. Called the "Father of Atomic Physics."
rutherford.lesson: The atom was almost entirely empty.

minkowski.name: Minkowski
minkowski.detail: Expressed relativity as four-dimensional spacetime combining time and space. Was also Einstein's teacher.
minkowski.lesson: Space and time became a single stage.

schwarzschild.name: Schwarzschild
schwarzschild.detail: While serving in World War I, derived an exact solution of general relativity. Died of illness soon after.
schwarzschild.lesson: An equation solved on the battlefield predicted black holes.

meitner.name: Lise Meitner
meitner.detail: Gave the theoretical explanation of nuclear fission. The Nobel Prize went only to Hahn, and the credit became a subject of debate.
meitner.lesson: Later generations questioned whether credit was given correctly.

noether.name: Emmy Noether
noether.detail: Showed Noether's theorem, that every symmetry implies a conservation law. It underlies modern physics.
noether.lesson: A view through symmetry revealed the essence of physical laws.

born.name: Max Born
born.detail: Proposed the probabilistic interpretation of the wave function and contributed to the development of quantum mechanics.
born.lesson: He read the wave function as expressing probability.

debroglie.name: de Broglie
debroglie.detail: Proposed the matter-wave idea that particles such as electrons also have wave properties.
debroglie.lesson: A noble student who thought particles have waves.

pauli.name: Pauli
pauli.detail: Proposed the Pauli exclusion principle, explaining electron behavior and atomic structure. Also predicted the neutrino.
pauli.lesson: A principle of "prohibition" underpins the stability of matter.

fermi.name: Fermi
fermi.detail: Built the first nuclear reactor and the theory of beta decay. His name also lives on in the Fermi paradox, "Where is everybody?"
fermi.lesson: A physicist skilled in both calculation and experiment.

dirac.name: Dirac
dirac.detail: Derived the relativistic equation of the electron and predicted antiparticles (the positron).

oppenheimer_c.name: Oppenheimer
oppenheimer_c.detail: In 1939 showed the theory that a giant star collapses under gravity into a black hole. Later led the Manhattan Project.
oppenheimer_c.lesson: A theorist of stars' ends also led the development of nuclear weapons.

bethe.name: Bethe
bethe.detail: Showed in theory that the energy source of stars is hydrogen fusion. Won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1967.
bethe.lesson: He solved by calculation how stars shine.

yukawa.name: Hideki Yukawa
yukawa.detail: Predicted the particle mediating the nuclear force (the meson) and in 1949 became the first Japanese Nobel laureate (Physics).
yukawa.lesson: With paper and pencil, he predicted a new particle.

tomonaga.name: Sin-Itiro Tomonaga
tomonaga.detail: Completed the "renormalization theory" of quantum electrodynamics and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1965.
tomonaga.lesson: He overcame the difficulty of infinities with theoretical ingenuity.

alvarez.name: Luis Alvarez
alvarez.detail: With his son Walter, proposed the asteroid-impact theory of dinosaur extinction. Also studied the inside of pyramids with muons.
alvarez.lesson: He took on mysteries outside his field with a physicist's eye.

feynman.name: Feynman
feynman.detail: Devised Feynman diagrams and won the Nobel Prize for quantum electrodynamics. Also known for his skillful teaching.
feynman.lesson: He showed difficult things with simple pictures.

nambu.name: Yoichiro Nambu
nambu.detail: Introduced the theory of spontaneous symmetry breaking into particle physics and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2008.

gellmann.name: Gell-Mann
gellmann.detail: Proposed the existence of quarks and classified elementary particles. The name "quark" comes from Joyce's novel.
gellmann.lesson: He brought order to the particle zoo.

higgs.name: Higgs
higgs.detail: Proposed the mechanism that gives particles mass. The Higgs boson was found in 2012, and he won the Nobel Prize in Physics the next year.
higgs.lesson: After 48 years, the prediction was confirmed by experiment.

weinberg.name: Weinberg
weinberg.detail: Built the theory unifying electromagnetism and the weak force and won the Nobel Prize. Conveyed cosmology to the public in The First Three Minutes.
weinberg.lesson: He spoke of his specialized physics in plain words.

masukawa.name: Toshihide Maskawa
masukawa.detail: With Makoto Kobayashi, proposed the theory explaining CP violation and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2008.
masukawa.lesson: He approached why more matter than antimatter remained.

hutton.name: Hutton
hutton.detail: Held that strata formed slowly over long periods and introduced the concept of "deep time." The "Father of Modern Geology."
hutton.lesson: Earth's time is far longer than humans imagine.

linnaeus.name: Linnaeus
linnaeus.detail: Established binomial nomenclature naming organisms by genus and species, laying the foundation of taxonomy.

humboldt.name: Humboldt
humboldt.detail: Explored South America and showed the relations among climate, vegetation and altitude. Spread the view of nature as one connected whole.
humboldt.lesson: He saw that nature is one network.

cuvier.name: Cuvier
cuvier.detail: Showed from fossil studies that organisms existed in the past and went extinct. The "Father of Paleontology."
cuvier.lesson: He proved the fact of extinction from fossils.

anning.name: Mary Anning
anning.detail: Found fossils of ichthyosaurs and plesiosaurs in seaside cliffs and contributed to paleontology. At the time she was not fully recognized by the scientific community, partly for being a woman.
anning.lesson: A self-taught digger moved the scientific world.

lyell.name: Lyell
lyell.detail: In Principles of Geology, argued that the accumulation of changes seen today made Earth's history. Strongly influenced Darwin.
lyell.lesson: The extension of present processes explains the past.

wallace.name: Wallace
wallace.detail: Arrived at the idea of natural selection independently of Darwin and founded biogeography through surveys of the Malay Archipelago.
wallace.lesson: Different people reached the same conclusion separately.

haeckel.name: Haeckel
haeckel.detail: Spread evolutionary theory, drew trees of life, and coined the word "ecology."
haeckel.lesson: He showed the tree of life as a diagram.

wegener.name: Wegener
wegener.detail: Proposed continental drift, that continents move. Not accepted in his lifetime, he was later vindicated by plate tectonics.
wegener.lesson: An idea ahead of its time was recognized later.

leakey_m.name: Mary Leakey
leakey_m.detail: Greatly advanced the study of early humans, including finding bipedal footprints about 3.66 million years old at Laetoli, Tanzania.
leakey_m.lesson: Footprints proved how old humanity is.

miller.name: Stanley Miller
miller.detail: Showed that amino acids form in a discharge experiment modeling the early Earth and opened the study of the origin of life.
miller.lesson: The ingredients of life can be made naturally.

patterson.name: Clair Patterson
patterson.detail: Measured lead isotopes in meteorites and determined Earth's age as about 4.55 billion years. Later took on the problem of lead pollution.
patterson.lesson: A meteorite told us Earth's age.

margulis.name: Lynn Margulis
margulis.detail: Proposed the endosymbiotic theory that mitochondria and chloroplasts originate from bacteria that lived symbiotically in cells.
